Educational ecosystem · Coexistence and a culture of peace

Pedagogy and artificial intelligence for learning to live together.

TARA is an educational ecosystem for coexistence and a culture of peace that brings together training, school structures and a conversational component based on artificial intelligence. Implementation begins with school professionals and moves forward step by step to strengthen the relational skills of the whole school community.

What TARA is

Understand each other better. Care for relationships. Build coexistence.

TARA fits into the school's existing coexistence plan, tutoring, guidance and protocols. It doesn't create a parallel system. The AI works as scaffolding: it helps people pause, understand, explore and prepare to act. The decision stays with the people responsible.

Technology supports and facilitates. People assess, decide and act.

  • Pedagogy
  • Training
  • Resources
  • Conversational AI

Pedagogical innovation.

We combine training, resources and conversational support so that teachers and families can carry what they learn into everyday relationships and situations at school and at home.

Technological innovation.

We use conversational AI as support to reflect, rehearse ways of expressing ourselves and prepare conversations. Technology facilitates; people assess, decide and act.

Why TARA exists

Many schools already have professionals, knowledge and protocols. TARA aims to add time, structure and support.

Learning to live together shouldn't depend only on the resources of each school or family. TARA wants to bring tools for emotional education, communication and a culture of peace to diverse school communities. Our goal is to help more people practise these skills in their everyday lives. Through schools, we want this learning to reach more and more people and carry over into everyday relationships, inside and outside school.

Professionals Knowledge Protocols Resources + time, structure and support Everyday practice

TARA does not aim to add work for schools. It wants to make the work they already need to do easier, with pedagogical judgement, and to strengthen the skills they already have.

Some figures that show schools need support

  • 84.6%of teachers cite a lack of resources (time, means, support) as a barrier to intervening in bullying.
  • 46.9%cite a lack of training.
  • 59.6%believe schools, in general, only sometimes respond appropriately to bullying.

Source: Fundación Mutua Madrileña and Fundación ANAR, 8th Report on Bullying in Schools (VIII Informe de Acoso Escolar en Centros Educativos), 2025-2026 school year, September 2026. Answers from 412 teachers at 236 schools across several Spanish regions. The figures describe an educational problem, not results of TARA.

Everyday situations where TARA aims to be useful.

Preparing a difficult meeting

“I have to talk to an upset family and I don't know how to start.” TARA can help organise what happened and prepare a respectful opening.

Conflict in the classroom

“Two students argue constantly and the group is divided.” TARA can help the teacher prepare listening questions and possible educational steps.

Managing your own response

“I left class today feeling very frustrated and I'm afraid I'll snap.” TARA can help you pause, recognise needs and choose how to act.

When talking is hard

“My daughter comes home from school, shuts herself in her room and won't talk.” TARA can help prepare a conversation that respects her pace.

Agreements about screens

“Every afternoon we argue about the phone.” TARA can help identify needs and think of proposals for family agreements.

Talking to the school

“I feel the school isn't listening to our concern.” TARA can help prepare a meeting and make a clear, respectful request.

Illustrative situations. Their availability will depend on the mode activated and the implementation phase; they are not real conversations from a pilot.

How it's implemented

Five levels, always with prior preparation.

Implementation begins with school professionals and moves up level by level, always with prior preparation. The 2027 pilot will start at level 1 and may gradually add other modes, only when the corresponding pedagogical, technical, organisational and protection conditions are met. No level is activated automatically.

  1. 01

    School professionals

    Teachers, tutoring, guidance, coexistence, leadership and other professional profiles.

    2027 Network
  2. 02

    Families

    Their own adult access, with specific information and resources.

    2027 Network · if the school decides so
  3. 03

    Whole-class educational use

    Activities led by responsible professionals.

    2027 Network · primary and secondary, if conditions are met
  4. 04

    Guided student work

    In pairs or small groups: supervised work on situations, cases, dialogues and educational activities.

    2027-28 school year · secondary
  5. 05

    Supervised individual use

    Direct interaction within a planned educational activity, during school hours, with an adult present, prior preparation and the protection circuit active.

    2027-28 school year · secondary

Protection

Protection is part of the educational design.

It doesn't diagnose or decide.

TARA does not diagnose, does not assess people, does not decide sanctions and does not replace guidance staff, specialist services or the school's protection procedures.

It works with what the person expresses.

TARA does not perform emotion recognition or attribute inner states as facts. When it offers vocabulary or a possible understanding, it frames it as an open hypothesis that the person can confirm, correct or reject.

It recognises its limits and connects with people.

TARA is designed to recognise when a situation goes beyond educational use and to point towards the people responsible at the school and their protocols. Students do not have free access: when they take part, it will be within school activities and with responsible adults.

Frequently asked questions

What schools and institutions often ask us.

Who is it for?

For the whole school community: school professionals (teaching, tutoring, guidance, coexistence and leadership), families and institutions that want to collaborate. Students join gradually, always with preparation, supervision and protection.

What does it bring to my school?

The implementation model includes tools for tutoring, guidance and coexistence, professional training and work with families, activated progressively according to each school's phase and level.

And to families?

Their own adult access, with specific information and resources to better understand what your son or daughter is going through and prepare the conversations that are hard to have at home.

What stage is TARA at?

TARA is preparing a pilot in schools for 2027. The aim will be to test its educational usefulness, uptake, feasibility and safety before extending its use. We do not present as proven results what are still evaluation objectives, nor as closed any institutional agreements that are still being explored.

Will students take part in the pilot?

The pilot starts with school professionals. In 2027, within the Partner Schools Network, teacher-led whole-class activities (level 3) may be considered in primary and secondary schools, after the necessary checks; in early years, work is done with professionals and families. From the 2027-28 school year, guided work in pairs or small groups (level 4) and supervised individual use (level 5) may be added in secondary schools, the latter only from age 14 and with specific protection conditions. Planning these modes does not mean they will necessarily be activated in every school.

How do I get in touch?

Through the contact form. A person from the team will reply.

Privacy & protection

What we keep and what we don't.

TARA is designed for the school community. Each profile has its own kind of access, and students take part only in the modes the school has activated, under the corresponding conditions of preparation, supervision and protection. Full privacy policy →

Encrypted connections

Information travels over encrypted connections, and access is restricted according to the roles and conditions defined for each mode. No data sales, advertising or commercial tracking.

GDPR and child-protection rules

European regulation and Spanish law for minors.

Age of use

When students take part, it will only be in school activities and with responsible adults. Each school decides the ages for group activities; individual use will be from age 14.

2027 pilot

2027 pilot: learn, evaluate and improve

In 2027 we are creating the TARA Partner Schools Network: up to 20 pioneering schools that explore, evaluate and co-design TARA with us.

For 2027, TARA is preparing a first pilot in schools that will start with school professionals and may gradually add other modes of use, under the established conditions of preparation, supervision and protection. The project includes evaluating its educational usefulness, feasibility, safety and implementation conditions. We are also exploring collaboration with universities to carry out independent scientific research that can study its results and guide its future expansion.

Outlook 2027-2031

The initial pilot is part of the 2027–2031 Strategic Plan, which aims to gradually expand TARA's implementation and develop a system that makes it easier for a growing number of schools to adopt it. Our goal is to build a scalable model that maintains pedagogical quality, protection safeguards and human responsibility.
